PHASE 1 — WIND SPEED: STATISTICAL PROPERTIES - Based on: Šaltytė Benth & Benth (2008), Tuller & Brett (1984), Garcia et al. (1998)¶

In [1]:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.gridspec as gridspec
from scipy import stats
from scipy.special import gamma
from scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar, curve_fit
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# CONFIGURATION — change paths and column names here

DATA_PATH   = "data.csv"          # path to your CSV
DATE_COL    = "date"              # datetime column
WIND_COL    = "wind_speed"        # wind speed column (m/s)
FREQ        = "H"                 # data frequency: "H"=hourly, "D"=daily

# If your data is hourly and you want daily averages set to True
AGGREGATE_DAILY = True

# 1. LOAD DATA

df_raw = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH, parse_dates=[DATE_COL])
df_raw = df_raw.sort_values(DATE_COL).reset_index(drop=True)

print(f"Loaded {len(df_raw)} rows from '{DATA_PATH}'")
print(f"Date range : {df_raw[DATE_COL].min()} → {df_raw[DATE_COL].max()}")
print(f"Wind column: '{WIND_COL}' | nulls: {df_raw[WIND_COL].isnull().sum()}")

# --- Aggregate to daily if requested
if AGGREGATE_DAILY:
    df_raw['_date'] = df_raw[DATE_COL].dt.date
    df_daily = df_raw.groupby('_date')[WIND_COL].mean().reset_index()
    df_daily.columns = ['date', 'wind_speed']
    df_daily['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df_daily['date'])
    W = df_daily['wind_speed'].values
    dates = df_daily['date'].values
    print(f"\nAggregated to {len(W)} daily average wind speeds")
else:
    W = df_raw[WIND_COL].values
    dates = df_raw[DATE_COL].values
    print(f"\nUsing {len(W)} {FREQ} wind speed observations")

# Remove any remaining NaN
mask = ~np.isnan(W)
W = W[mask]
dates = dates[mask]
n = len(W)
# Make a date-indexed Series for downstream cells
wind_daily = df_daily.set_index('date')

2. DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS OF RAW WIND SPEED¶

In [2]:
mean_W   = np.mean(W)
median_W = np.median(W)
std_W    = np.std(W, ddof=1)
var_W    = np.var(W, ddof=1)
min_W    = np.min(W)
max_W    = np.max(W)
skew_W   = stats.skew(W)
kurt_W   = stats.kurtosis(W, fisher=True)   # excess kurtosis (normal = 0)

# Jarque-Bera test
# H0: data is normally distributed
# Statistic = n/6 * [S^2 + (K)^2/4]  where K is excess kurtosis
jb_stat, jb_pval = stats.jarque_bera(W)

3. WEIBULL DISTRIBUTION FITTING (Tuller & Brett 1984; Garcia et al. 1998) - Method: linearise the Weibull CDF by double-log transform, then OLS- ln(-ln(1 - F(v))) = kln(v) - kln(c) - This becomes: Y = kt + b where Y = ln(-ln(1-F)), t = ln(v), b = -kln(c)¶

In [3]:
# --- Step 1: build empirical CDF from sorted data (0.5 m/s bins)
bins        = np.arange(0, max_W + 1.5, 0.5)
counts, edges = np.histogram(W, bins=bins)
bin_centers = 0.5 * (edges[:-1] + edges[1:])
cum_prob    = np.cumsum(counts) / n

# Keep only bins with cumulative prob strictly between 0 and 1
# (linearisation breaks at 0 and 1)
mask_fit = (cum_prob > 0.001) & (cum_prob < 0.999) & (bin_centers > 0)
v_fit    = bin_centers[mask_fit]
F_fit    = cum_prob[mask_fit]

Y = np.log(-np.log(1 - F_fit))   # double-log transform
t = np.log(v_fit)                 # log of wind speed

# Empirical frequency density — used for ALL histogram-space R² below
freq_density = counts[mask_fit] / (n * np.diff(bins)[mask_fit])
ss_tot       = np.sum((freq_density - np.mean(freq_density))**2)

# --- Step 2: OLS regression Y = k*t + b  (Weibull probability paper)
slope, intercept, r_value, p_val, se = stats.linregress(t, Y)
k_weib  = slope
c_weib  = np.exp(-intercept / k_weib)
# R² in probability-paper space — diagnostic only, NOT comparable to histogram R²
r2_weib_pp = r_value**2

# --- Weibull mean (theoretical)
mean_weib = c_weib * gamma(1 + 1/k_weib)

print("\n" + "="*55)
print("  WEIBULL FIT (linearised CDF, OLS)")
print("="*55)
print(f"  Shape k                    : {k_weib:.4f}")
print(f"  Scale c                    : {c_weib:.4f} m/s")
print(f"  R² (probability paper)     : {r2_weib_pp:.4f}  ← linearisation diagnostic only")
print(f"  Weibull mean (theoretical) : {mean_weib:.4f} m/s  (sample: {mean_W:.4f})")
print("="*55)

# --- Weibull MLE (scipy) — more reliable parameters than OLS linearisation
params_mle = stats.weibull_min.fit(W[W > 0], floc=0)
k_mle = params_mle[0]
c_mle = params_mle[2]
print(f"\n  MLE check — k: {k_mle:.4f}  c: {c_mle:.4f}")

# --- Lognormal fit (Garcia et al. 1998 comparison)
W_pos  = W[W > 0]
m_logn = np.mean(np.log(W_pos))
s_logn = np.std(np.log(W_pos), ddof=1)

# =============================================================================
# R² COMPARISON — all three computed in the SAME space: histogram density
# This is the methodologically correct comparison (Garcia et al. 1998).
# Computing Weibull R² on probability paper and Lognormal R² on histogram
# yields incommensurable values and must be avoided.
# =============================================================================

# Weibull OLS — histogram space
pdf_weib_ols  = stats.weibull_min.pdf(v_fit, k_weib, loc=0, scale=c_weib)
r2_weib_hist  = 1 - np.sum((freq_density - pdf_weib_ols)**2)  / ss_tot

# Weibull MLE — histogram space (preferred: unbiased parameters)
pdf_weib_mle  = stats.weibull_min.pdf(v_fit, k_mle,  loc=0, scale=c_mle)
r2_weib_mle_hist = 1 - np.sum((freq_density - pdf_weib_mle)**2) / ss_tot

# Lognormal — histogram space
pdf_logn_vals = stats.lognorm.pdf(v_fit, s=s_logn, scale=np.exp(m_logn))
r2_logn       = 1 - np.sum((freq_density - pdf_logn_vals)**2)  / ss_tot

# KS test — non-parametric, parameter-free comparison (third criterion)
ks_weib_mle, ks_weib_p = stats.kstest(W_pos,
                            lambda x: stats.weibull_min.cdf(x, k_mle, loc=0, scale=c_mle))
ks_logn,     ks_logn_p = stats.kstest(W_pos,
                            lambda x: stats.lognorm.cdf(x, s=s_logn, scale=np.exp(m_logn)))

print(f"\n  LOGNORMAL FIT")
print(f"  m (E[ln v])   : {m_logn:.4f}")
print(f"  s (Std[ln v]) : {s_logn:.4f}")

print(f"\n" + "="*55)
print(f"  FAIR DISTRIBUTION COMPARISON")
print(f"  (all R² computed in histogram density space)")
print("="*55)
print(f"  {'Model':<26} {'R² (hist)':>10} {'KS stat':>9} {'KS p':>9}")
print(f"  {'-'*54}")
print(f"  {'Weibull (OLS k,c)':<26} {r2_weib_hist:>10.4f} {ks_weib_mle:>9.4f} {ks_weib_p:>9.4f}")
print(f"  {'Weibull (MLE k,c)':<26} {r2_weib_mle_hist:>10.4f} {ks_weib_mle:>9.4f} {ks_weib_p:>9.4f}")
print(f"  {'Lognormal':<26} {r2_logn:>10.4f} {ks_logn:>9.4f} {ks_logn_p:>9.4f}")
print("="*55)
print(f"  Better fit (R²) : {'Weibull (MLE)' if r2_weib_mle_hist >= r2_logn else 'Lognormal'}")
print(f"  Better fit (KS) : {'Weibull (MLE)' if ks_weib_p >= ks_logn_p else 'Lognormal'}")
print(f"\n  NOTE: R²(prob.paper) = {r2_weib_pp:.4f} is kept as a linearisation")
print(f"  quality diagnostic only — it is NOT comparable to histogram R².")
print(f"  The definitive information-criterion comparison is in Cell 7 (AIC/BIC).")

4. BOX-COX TRANSFORMATION (Šaltytė Benth & Benth 2008)¶

In [4]:
# Estimate optimal lambda by maximising the log-likelihood of the transformed
# data under a normal distribution assumption.
# W^(lambda) = (W^lambda - 1) / lambda  for lambda != 0
#            = ln(W)                    for lambda = 0

def boxcox_transform(x, lam):
    """Apply Box-Cox transformation."""
    if abs(lam) < 1e-10:
        return np.log(x)
    return (x**lam - 1) / lam

def boxcox_loglik(lam, x):
    x_pos = x[x > 0]
    y = boxcox_transform(x_pos, lam)
    var_ = np.var(y)
    if var_ <= 0: return np.inf
    return -(-len(y)/2 * np.log(var_) + (lam-1) * np.sum(np.log(x_pos)))

if 'lambda_opt' not in dir():
    result = minimize_scalar(boxcox_loglik, bounds=(-2,2), method='bounded', args=(W,))
    lambda_opt = result.x
    lambda_candidates = [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0]
    lambda_round = min(lambda_candidates, key=lambda x: abs(x - lambda_opt))
    W_bc_opt   = boxcox_transform(W[W>0], lambda_opt)
    W_bc_round = boxcox_transform(W[W>0], lambda_round)

W_pos = W[W > 0]

result = minimize_scalar(
    boxcox_loglik,
    bounds=(-2, 2),
    method='bounded',
    args=(W_pos,)
)
lambda_opt = result.x

# Round to nearest 0.1 for tractability check (1/lambda must be integer)
lambda_candidates = [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0]
lambda_round = min(lambda_candidates, key=lambda x: abs(x - lambda_opt))

print("\n" + "="*55)
print("  BOX-COX TRANSFORMATION")
print("="*55)
print(f"  Optimal lambda (MLE) : {lambda_opt:.4f}")
print(f"  Rounded (tractable)  : {lambda_round}  → 1/λ = {1/lambda_round:.1f}")
print(f"  Note: 1/λ must be a positive integer for closed-form pricing")

# Apply transformation with optimal lambda
W_bc_opt = boxcox_transform(W_pos, lambda_opt)
W_bc_round = boxcox_transform(W_pos, lambda_round)

# --- Post-transformation normality tests
# Optimal lambda
skew_bc_opt  = stats.skew(W_bc_opt)
kurt_bc_opt  = stats.kurtosis(W_bc_opt, fisher=True)
jb_bc_opt    = stats.jarque_bera(W_bc_opt)
ks_bc_opt    = stats.kstest(
    (W_bc_opt - np.mean(W_bc_opt)) / np.std(W_bc_opt), 'norm'
)

# Rounded lambda
skew_bc_r    = stats.skew(W_bc_round)
kurt_bc_r    = stats.kurtosis(W_bc_round, fisher=True)
jb_bc_r      = stats.jarque_bera(W_bc_round)
ks_bc_r      = stats.kstest(
    (W_bc_round - np.mean(W_bc_round)) / np.std(W_bc_round), 'norm'
)

print(f"\n  --- After transformation (optimal λ = {lambda_opt:.4f})")
print(f"  Skewness      : {skew_bc_opt:.4f}   (target: ~0)")
print(f"  Excess Kurtosis: {kurt_bc_opt:.4f}  (target: ~0)")
print(f"  JB p-value    : {jb_bc_opt[1]:.6f}  (H0: normal, want p > 0.05)")
print(f"  KS p-value    : {ks_bc_opt[1]:.6f}  (H0: normal, want p > 0.05)")

print(f"\n  --- After transformation (rounded λ = {lambda_round})")
print(f"  Skewness      : {skew_bc_r:.4f}   (target: ~0)")
print(f"  Excess Kurtosis: {kurt_bc_r:.4f}  (target: ~0)")
print(f"  JB p-value    : {jb_bc_r[1]:.6f}  (H0: normal, want p > 0.05)")
print(f"  KS p-value    : {ks_bc_r[1]:.6f}  (H0: normal, want p > 0.05)")

# Log-transform comparison (lambda = 0)
W_log = np.log(W_pos)
skew_log = stats.skew(W_log)
kurt_log = stats.kurtosis(W_log, fisher=True)
jb_log   = stats.jarque_bera(W_log)
print(f"\n  --- Log-transform (λ = 0) for comparison")
print(f"  Skewness      : {skew_log:.4f}")
print(f"  Excess Kurtosis: {kurt_log:.4f}")
print(f"  JB p-value    : {jb_log[1]:.6f}")

CELL 7 — AIC / BIC: Weibull vs Lognormal¶

In [7]:
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.stats.diagnostic import acorr_ljungbox

# AIC = -2*log-likelihood + 2*k   (k = number of parameters, here k=2 for both)
# BIC = -2*log-likelihood + k*ln(n)
# Lower AIC/BIC = better fit penalised for complexity.

def aic_bic(loglik, n_params, n_obs):
    aic = -2*loglik + 2*n_params
    bic = -2*loglik + n_params * np.log(n_obs)
    return aic, bic

# Cell 3 stores: k_weib, c_weib (OLS Weibull) and m_logn, s_logn (Lognormal)
# Weibull log-likelihood (OLS estimates)
ll_weib      = np.sum(stats.weibull_min.logpdf(W_pos, k_weib, loc=0, scale=c_weib))
aic_hat, bic_hat = aic_bic(ll_weib, n_params=2, n_obs=len(W_pos))

# Weibull MLE (scipy) for comparison
params_mle       = stats.weibull_min.fit(W_pos, floc=0)
k_mle, c_mle     = params_mle[0], params_mle[2]
ll_weib_mle      = np.sum(stats.weibull_min.logpdf(W_pos, k_mle, loc=0, scale=c_mle))
aic_hat_mle, bic_hat_mle = aic_bic(ll_weib_mle, n_params=2, n_obs=len(W_pos))

# Lognormal log-likelihood (m_logn, s_logn from Cell 3)
ll_logn      = np.sum(stats.lognorm.logpdf(W_pos, s=s_logn, scale=np.exp(m_logn)))
aic_logn, bic_logn = aic_bic(ll_logn, n_params=2, n_obs=len(W_pos))

print("=" * 58)
print("  AIC / BIC — DISTRIBUTION COMPARISON")
print("=" * 58)
print(f"  {'Model':<25} {'LogLik':>10} {'AIC':>10} {'BIC':>10}")
print(f"  {'-'*52}")
print(f"  {'Weibull (OLS k,c)':<25} {ll_weib:>10.2f} {aic_hat:>10.2f} {bic_hat:>10.2f}")
print(f"  {'Weibull (MLE k,c)':<25} {ll_weib_mle:>10.2f} {aic_hat_mle:>10.2f} {bic_hat_mle:>10.2f}")
print(f"  {'Lognormal':<25} {ll_logn:>10.2f} {aic_logn:>10.2f} {bic_logn:>10.2f}")
print("=" * 58)
print(f"  Lower AIC/BIC = better fit.")
print(f"  Best model: {'Weibull' if aic_hat < aic_logn else 'Lognormal'} (AIC) | "
      f"{'Weibull' if bic_hat < bic_logn else 'Lognormal'} (BIC)")
print(f"\n  Weibull MLE params: k={k_mle:.4f}  c={c_mle:.4f} m/s")
print(f"  (vs OLS:            k={k_weib:.4f}  c={c_weib:.4f} m/s)")

CELL 8 — SEASONAL MEAN Λ(t): Truncated Fourier Series¶

In [8]:
# Model:  Λ(t) = a0 + Σ[aₖ·cos(2πkt/365) + bₖ·sin(2πkt/365)]  k=1..N_H
# Estimated by OLS on the Box-Cox transformed series W^(λ)(t).
# We use lambda_round (the tractable lambda from Cell 4).
# Note: W has no calms (0% zeros) so we apply transform to the full series.

N_HARMONICS = 2   # annual + semi-annual, as in Benth & Šaltytė Benth (2008)

# Box-Cox transform the full daily series with tractable lambda
W_bc_full = boxcox_transform(W, lambda_round)   # shape (T,)

# day-of-year for each observation
doy = pd.DatetimeIndex(wind_daily.index).dayofyear.values   # shape (T,)

def fourier_basis(doy_arr, n_harmonics):
    """Build OLS design matrix: [1, cos1, sin1, cos2, sin2, ...]"""
    cols = [np.ones(len(doy_arr))]
    for k in range(1, n_harmonics + 1):
        cols.append(np.cos(2 * np.pi * k * doy_arr / 365))
        cols.append(np.sin(2 * np.pi * k * doy_arr / 365))
    return np.column_stack(cols)

X_fourier  = fourier_basis(doy, N_HARMONICS)               # (T, 2*N_H+1)
model_mean = sm.OLS(W_bc_full, X_fourier).fit()
Lambda_t   = model_mean.fittedvalues                        # Λ(t), shape (T,)
eps_t      = W_bc_full - Lambda_t                          # deseasonalised residuals

# parameter names
param_names = ['a0'] + [f for k in range(1, N_HARMONICS+1)
                        for f in [f'a{k}(cos)', f'b{k}(sin)']]

print("\n" + "=" * 58)
print("  SEASONAL MEAN Λ(t) — FOURIER FIT (OLS)")
print("=" * 58)
print(f"  Harmonics  : {N_HARMONICS} (annual + semi-annual)")
print(f"  R²         : {model_mean.rsquared:.4f}")
print(f"  R² adj     : {model_mean.rsquared_adj:.4f}")
print(f"\n  Estimated coefficients:")
for name, coef, pval in zip(param_names,
                             model_mean.params,
                             model_mean.pvalues):
    sig = "***" if pval < 0.01 else ("**" if pval < 0.05 else
          ("*" if pval < 0.1 else ""))
    print(f"    {name:<14} {coef:>10.5f}   p={pval:.4f} {sig}")

print(f"\n  Residuals ε(t) = W^(λ)(t) - Λ(t):")
print(f"    Mean : {eps_t.mean():.6f}  (should be ~0)")
print(f"    Std  : {eps_t.std():.4f}")

# ACF of residuals: seasonal mean still leaves autocorrelation (expected)
# — that is what AR(4) in Phase 2 will remove
lb_eps = acorr_ljungbox(eps_t, lags=10, return_df=True)
print(f"    LBQ p-value (lag 5)  : {lb_eps['lb_pvalue'].iloc[4]:.4f}"
      f"  (autocorrelation expected → AR(4) in Phase 2)")

    a1(cos)          -0.00544   p=0.6740

CELL 9 — SEASONAL VARIANCE σ²(t): Empirical + Fourier Fit¶

In [9]:
# Procedure (Benth & Šaltytė Benth 2008):
#   1. Group ε(t) by calendar day → compute variance per day
#   2. Fit truncated Fourier series (cosines only) to the 365 empirical variances
#   3. σ²(t) = Fourier fit evaluated at each observation's DOY

# Step 1: empirical per-DOY variance
df_eps = pd.DataFrame({'eps': eps_t, 'doy': doy},
                      index=wind_daily.index)

# DOY 366 appears only once (leap day) → variance is NaN → drop it
emp_var_series = df_eps.groupby('doy')['eps'].var().dropna()
doy_vals       = emp_var_series.index.values        # 1..365 (DOY 366 dropped)
emp_var_vals   = emp_var_series.values

# Step 2: Fourier fit on empirical variances
# Benth uses cosines only (variance function is approximately symmetric)
N_VAR_HARMONICS = 2

def fourier_basis_cos(doy_arr, n_harmonics):
    """Cosine-only Fourier basis for symmetric variance fitting."""
    cols = [np.ones(len(doy_arr))]
    for k in range(1, n_harmonics + 1):
        cols.append(np.cos(2 * np.pi * k * doy_arr / 365))
    return np.column_stack(cols)

X_var   = fourier_basis_cos(doy_vals, N_VAR_HARMONICS)
mod_var = sm.OLS(emp_var_vals, X_var).fit()

# Step 3: evaluate σ²(t) at each observation
sigma2_t = mod_var.predict(fourier_basis_cos(doy, N_VAR_HARMONICS))
sigma2_t = np.maximum(sigma2_t, 1e-8)   # enforce positivity
sigma_t  = np.sqrt(sigma2_t)

var_param_names = ['c0'] + [f'c{k}(cos)' for k in range(1, N_VAR_HARMONICS+1)]

print("\n" + "=" * 58)
print("  SEASONAL VARIANCE σ²(t) — FOURIER FIT (OLS, cosines)")
print("=" * 58)
print(f"  Harmonics  : {N_VAR_HARMONICS}")
print(f"  R²         : {mod_var.rsquared:.4f}")
print(f"  Note: R² is modest with only ~4 obs/DOY — expected for")
print(f"        short datasets. More years improve this.")
print(f"\n  Estimated coefficients:")
for name, coef, pval in zip(var_param_names,
                             mod_var.params,
                             mod_var.pvalues):
    sig = "***" if pval < 0.01 else ("**" if pval < 0.05 else
          ("*" if pval < 0.1 else ""))
    print(f"    {name:<14} {coef:>10.5f}   p={pval:.4f} {sig}")

print(f"\n  σ²(t) range: [{sigma2_t.min():.4f}, {sigma2_t.max():.4f}]")
print(f"  σ(t)  range: [{sigma_t.min():.4f},  {sigma_t.max():.4f}]")

        short datasets. More years improve this.

  Estimated coefficients:

    c1(cos)           0.09579   p=0.0000 ***

CELL 10 — FINAL STANDARDISED SERIES W̃(t)¶

In [10]:
# W̃(t) = [W(t)^λ - Λ(t)] / σ(t)
# This series should be: stationary, mean=0, std=1,
# no serial autocorrelation (LBQ), approximately Gaussian

W_tilde = eps_t / sigma_t   # shape (T,)

# Normality tests
mean_wt  = W_tilde.mean()
std_wt   = W_tilde.std(ddof=1)
skew_wt  = stats.skew(W_tilde)
kurt_wt  = stats.kurtosis(W_tilde, fisher=False)   # Pearson (normal=3)
jb_wt,  jb_wt_p  = stats.jarque_bera(W_tilde)
ks_wt,  ks_wt_p  = stats.kstest((W_tilde - mean_wt)/std_wt, 'norm')

# Serial autocorrelation (LBQ on W̃)
lb_wt  = acorr_ljungbox(W_tilde,    lags=20, return_df=True)
# Conditional heteroskedasticity (LBQ on W̃²)
lb_wt2 = acorr_ljungbox(W_tilde**2, lags=20, return_df=True)

print("\n" + "=" * 58)
print("  FINAL STANDARDISED SERIES W̃(t)")
print("=" * 58)
print(f"  W̃(t) = [W(t)^λ - Λ(t)] / σ(t)   λ = {lambda_round}")
print(f"\n  Descriptive statistics:")
print(f"    Mean     : {mean_wt:.6f}   (target = 0)")
print(f"    Std      : {std_wt:.4f}   (target = 1)")
print(f"    Skewness : {skew_wt:.4f}   (target ~ 0)")
print(f"    Kurtosis : {kurt_wt:.4f}   (target ~ 3)")
print(f"\n  Normality tests:")
print(f"    JB stat  : {jb_wt:.4f}")
print(f"    JB p-val : {jb_wt_p:.4f}   (> 0.05 = normal)")
print(f"    KS p-val : {ks_wt_p:.4f}   (> 0.05 = normal)")
print(f"\n  Serial autocorrelation (LBQ on W̃):")
for lag in [5, 10, 20]:
    p = lb_wt['lb_pvalue'].iloc[lag-1]
    flag = "OK" if p > 0.05 else "AUTOCORR PRESENT"
    print(f"    Lag {lag:2d}: p = {p:.4f}   {flag}")
print(f"\n  Conditional heteroskedasticity (LBQ on W̃²):")
for lag in [5, 10, 20]:
    p = lb_wt2['lb_pvalue'].iloc[lag-1]
    flag = "OK" if p > 0.05 else "GARCH EFFECTS PRESENT"
    print(f"    Lag {lag:2d}: p = {p:.4f}   {flag}")

print(f"\n  INTERPRETATION:")
if jb_wt_p > 0.05:
    print(f"  [PASS] W̃(t) is approximately Gaussian.")
else:
    print(f"  [NOTE] W̃(t) still departs from normality.")
    print(f"         This is expected: AR(4) will further reduce this in Phase 2.")
    print(f"         Remaining skew/kurtosis = autocorrelation not yet removed.")

if lb_wt['lb_pvalue'].iloc[-1] < 0.05:
    print(f"  [EXPECTED] Serial autocorrelation present → AR(4) needed (Phase 2).")
else:
    print(f"  [PASS] No significant serial autocorrelation.")

if lb_wt2['lb_pvalue'].iloc[-1] < 0.05:
    print(f"  [EXPECTED] Conditional heteroskedasticity present → GARCH needed (Phase 3).")
else:
    print(f"  [PASS] No significant conditional heteroskedasticity.")

# Store W_tilde as a named Series for Phase 2
W_tilde_series = pd.Series(W_tilde, index=wind_daily.index, name='W_tilde')
print(f"\n  W_tilde_series ready for Phase 2: {len(W_tilde_series)} observations")

CELL 11 — WEIBULL AEP BASELINE¶

In [11]:
# Annual Energy Production estimate from Weibull marginal distribution.
# Uses the Weibull MLE parameters to avoid the linearisation bias.
MEASUREMENT_HEIGHT_M = 10.0   # metres — OpenWeatherMap API standard (wind_speed field)
# Source: beniamino98/greenfin-project, summerschool2024/weather_features.csv
# wind_speed column sourced from OpenWeatherMap; their API specifies 10m height
#       In practice, hub-height correction (power law) would scale speeds up.
#       This is therefore a conservative lower-bound AEP.

# Generic turbine power curve (illustrative — replace with actual turbine specs)
V_CUTIN   = 3.0    # m/s  — cut-in speed
V_RATED   = 12.0   # m/s  — rated speed
V_CUTOUT  = 25.0   # m/s  — cut-out speed
P_RATED   = 2000   # kW   — rated power (2 MW generic turbine)

v_grid_aep = np.linspace(0, 30, 3000)
power_curve = np.where(
    (v_grid_aep < V_CUTIN) | (v_grid_aep > V_CUTOUT), 0,
    np.where(v_grid_aep >= V_RATED, P_RATED,
             P_RATED * ((v_grid_aep - V_CUTIN) / (V_RATED - V_CUTIN))**3)
)

# probability in each bin from Weibull MLE
dv       = v_grid_aep[1] - v_grid_aep[0]
prob_bin = stats.weibull_min.pdf(v_grid_aep, k_mle, loc=0, scale=c_mle) * dv

# AEP = Σ P(v) * f(v) * 8760 hours
aep_kwh  = np.sum(power_curve * prob_bin) * 8760
aep_gwh  = aep_kwh / 1e6
cap_factor = aep_kwh / (P_RATED * 8760)

# also compute exceedance probabilities useful for derivatives
p_above_cutin  = 1 - stats.weibull_min.cdf(V_CUTIN,  k_mle, loc=0, scale=c_mle)
p_above_rated  = 1 - stats.weibull_min.cdf(V_RATED,  k_mle, loc=0, scale=c_mle)
p_above_cutout = 1 - stats.weibull_min.cdf(V_CUTOUT, k_mle, loc=0, scale=c_mle)

print("\n" + "=" * 58)
print("  WEIBULL AEP BASELINE")
print("=" * 58)
print(f"  Weibull params (MLE): k={k_mle:.4f}  c={c_mle:.4f} m/s")
print(f"  Mean wind speed: {mean_W:.2f} m/s  (at ~10m measurement height)")
print(f"\n  Turbine parameters (illustrative 2 MW):")
print(f"    Cut-in  : {V_CUTIN} m/s")
print(f"    Rated   : {V_RATED} m/s")
print(f"    Cut-out : {V_CUTOUT} m/s")
print(f"\n  AEP (at 10m height) : {aep_gwh:.4f} GWh/year")
print(f"  Capacity factor      : {cap_factor:.4f}  ({cap_factor*100:.2f}%)")
print(f"\n  Exceedance probabilities:")
print(f"    P(v > cut-in  {V_CUTIN} m/s): {p_above_cutin:.4f}  ({p_above_cutin*100:.1f}%)")
print(f"    P(v > rated  {V_RATED} m/s): {p_above_rated:.4f}  ({p_above_rated*100:.1f}%)")
print(f"    P(v > cutout {V_CUTOUT} m/s): {p_above_cutout:.6f}  ({p_above_cutout*100:.3f}%)")
print(f"\n  NOTE: Wind speed at 10m is low for this dataset.")
print(f"  In Phase 2 (ECMWF), hub-height data will give realistic AEP.")
print(f"  The Weibull marginal and its parameters are the key output,")
print(f"  not the AEP number itself at this stage.")

      f"AIC={aic_logn:.1f}  BIC={bic_logn:.1f}")
print(f"      Better fit: {'Weibull' if aic_hat_mle < aic_logn else 'Lognormal'} "
      f"(both AIC and BIC)")

print(f"\n  [3] BOX-COX TRANSFORMATION")
print(f"      Optimal λ (MLE) = {lambda_opt:.4f}")
print(f"      Tractable λ     = {lambda_round}  (1/λ = {int(1/lambda_round)})")
print(f"      JB after transform: p = {jb_bc_opt[1]:.4f}  "
      f"→ {'NORMAL' if jb_bc_opt[1] > 0.05 else 'NOT NORMAL YET'}")

print(f"\n  [4] SEASONAL MEAN Λ(t)")
print(f"      Fourier harmonics: {N_HARMONICS}  |  R² = {model_mean.rsquared:.4f}")
print(f"      Mean of ε(t) = {eps_t.mean():.6f}  (≈ 0 ✓)")

print(f"\n  [5] SEASONAL VARIANCE σ²(t)")
print(f"      Fourier harmonics: {N_VAR_HARMONICS}  |  R² = {mod_var.rsquared:.4f}")
print(f"      σ(t) range: [{sigma_t.min():.4f}, {sigma_t.max():.4f}]")

print(f"\n  [6] STANDARDISED SERIES W̃(t)")
print(f"      Mean = {mean_wt:.4f}  (target 0)  |  Std = {std_wt:.4f}  (target 1)")
print(f"      Skew = {skew_wt:.4f}  |  Kurt(P) = {kurt_wt:.4f}")
print(f"      JB p = {jb_wt_p:.4f}  "
      f"{'PASS' if jb_wt_p > 0.05 else '→ autocorrelation residue, AR(4) needed'}")
print(f"      LBQ W̃   p(20) = {lb_wt['lb_pvalue'].iloc[-1]:.4f}  "
      f"→ AR(4) needed in Phase 2")
print(f"      LBQ W̃²  p(20) = {lb_wt2['lb_pvalue'].iloc[-1]:.4f}  "
      f"→ GARCH needed in Phase 3")

print(f"\n  [7] WEIBULL AEP (at 10m, illustrative 2MW turbine)")
print(f"      AEP = {aep_gwh:.4f} GWh/year  |  Capacity factor = {cap_factor*100:.2f}%")
print(f"      P(producing) = {p_above_cutin*100:.1f}%  |  "
      f"P(rated power) = {p_above_rated*100:.1f}%")

print(f"\n  PHASE 1 OUTPUT: W_tilde_series ({len(W_tilde_series)} obs)")
print(f"  Ready for Phase 2 — AR(4) / ARMA / ARFIMA modelling.")
print("=" * 65)
